extra_comparators.note: Post-hoc comparators evaluated with the frozen percentile; thresholds use the validation reliable-frame 90th percentile exactly as for the frozen comparators. They were not part of the pre-registered selection grid.

detection_latency.definition: A failure episode is a maximal run of >= 5 consecutive scored frames with IoU<0.5. Latency is the number of scored frames from the first frame of the first episode to the first frame of that episode at which the risk exceeds the validation-frozen threshold; episodes without an alarm are censored at their length and reported as missed. False alarms before the first episode are counted on reliable frames preceding it.

temporal_specificity.definition: Scored frames of each sequence are split into three equal-length thirds by position; specificity on reliable frames and alarm rate on reliable frames are macro-averaged over sequences that contain reliable frames in that third.

sensitivity.note: Post-hoc sensitivity analyses on the test partition; they inform robustness only and were not used to choose any parameter.

nanotrack.hierarchical_bootstrap_note: cases resampled with replacement, then sequences within each drawn case

stark.hierarchical_bootstrap_note: cases resampled with replacement, then sequences within each drawn case

conformal.statement: Split-conformal sequence-level calibration: let q_j be the 0.90 quantile of fused risk over the reliable frames of validation sequence j (j=1..n). For a miscoverage level delta, tau_delta is the ceil((n+1)(1-delta))-th smallest q_j. If a new sequence is exchangeable with the validation sequences, P(q_new <= tau_delta) >= 1-delta, i.e. with probability at least 1-delta its reliable-frame specificity at tau_delta is at least 0.90.

contour_chance_level.description: Monte Carlo chance level of the trimmed symmetric contour discrepancy between two independent random binary interior masks of the stated density on the 64x64 raster (2-pixel border empty), and its value between a mask and its translated copy.
